title: Liao kangkong: Characteristics
metaDescription: Liao kangkong is an open pollinated (no F1 label) kangkong variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Liao kangkong is an open pollinated (no F1 label) kangkong variety, also sold or known as East West kangkong Liao. It is not on the NSIC registry, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from East West Seed.

heroImage.alt: A farmer watering vegetable beds in Pulilan, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Liao kangkong is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for East West kangkong Liao, this is the same kangkong. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [kangkong variety finder](/crop-varieties/kangkong), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit kangkong fields most often: [golden apple snail](/pests/golden-apple-snail), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** 20 to 25 days after sowing.
**Fruit:** Leaves: narrow and green, on plants 30 to 40 cm tall.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: listed on East West Seed's Philippine website, no Philippine store, news or trial evidence was found. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual kangkong on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Liao kangkong

Upland kangkong grows from seed on dry beds, and lowland kangkong from cuttings in wet ground. Both regrow after each cutting. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Fertilizer for vegetables](/blog/fertilizer-for-vegetables-philippines).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.

items.q: Is East West kangkong Liao the same as Liao?
items.a: Yes. East West kangkong Liao is another name for Liao. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Liao?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
